newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian KB cuts charges for cross-border payments.
newsitem.headline: Belgian KB cuts charges for cross-border payments.

text.p: Belgian Kredietbank (KB) said on Wednesday it was cutting charges on cross-border payments from Thursday, anticipating planned European Union legislation to make such payments safer, quicker and cheaper.

"KB and (subsidiary) Credit General are the first banks able to announce a considerable cut in charges on incoming payments in Belgian francs from abroad," said Willy Baeten, product management leader of KB's foreign trade department.
KB will levy fixed charges for payments up to 350,000 francs, abandoning the current system of commission fees on the basis of more complex cumulative tranches.
The new EU directive, which is expected to be issued later this year, will compel financial institutions to meet a number of obligations aimed at improving consumer protection.

Once the directive, which will apply to payments of up to 50,000 European Currency units, is implemented, cross-border payments will have to be posted to the beneficiary's account no later than six banking days after the order is given, KB said.
If not, the banks in question will have to pay interest to either the principal, the beneficiary or both.
Baeten said about 80 percent of incoming payments in Belgian francs involved sums of less than 350,000 francs.
"So in most cases clients will profit from the cuts," he said.
He said KB could not cut charges on outgoing international payments or payments in foreign currencies as they were more complex to process and induced higher costs.
